sourcedFrom: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: This guide comes from Browning's own owner's manual for the BT-99, the single-barrel break-action trap gun. Two things set it apart. First, it has no safety at all. Browning says so plainly and tells you to keep the action open unless you are about to shoot, so an open action is your safety. Second, the field strip is only two parts: the forearm comes off, then the barrel lifts off the hinge pin. The hinge pin, barrel lugs and forearm bracket are hand-fitted surfaces that Browning wants kept under grease. That is where the real care goes on this gun.

steps.title: Top lever right, action fully open
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and keep your fingers off the trigger. Push the top lever all the way to the right and let the barrel drop so the action opens fully. Opening it only part way is not enough. Browning says it must open completely to reset the firing mechanism. The fit is tight, so you may need to pull down a little on the forearm to open the breech all the way.
steps.quote: Open the action by moving the top lever fully to the right.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading, step 1
steps.warn: WARNING: THE BT-99 DOES NOT HAVE A “SAFETY” MECHANISM.

steps.title: Take the shell off the extractor, then look through
steps.action: On the BT-99 the extractor lifts the shell up out of the chamber when the action opens. It does not throw it clear. So a live shell can still be sitting there, raised, waiting to be picked off. Take it out with your fingers. Then look into the chamber and through the barrel to be sure it is empty. Put the shell away from where you will be cleaning.
steps.quote: Remember, BT-99 models have an automatic extractor that lifts a shell, fired or unfired, from the chamber of the shotgun when the action is opened.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Unloading
steps.warn: ALWAYS INSPECT THE CHAMBER AND BARREL CAREFULLY AFTER UNLOADING TO BE SURE ANY LIVE SHELL IS CLEARED FROM THE FIREARM.

steps.title: Close it, brace the stock, lift the forearm latch
steps.action: With the gun empty, close the action. Rest the buttstock against your upper leg so the gun is held steady and pointed away. Lift the forearm takedown latch outward. The forearm has to come off first. The action must be closed for this, because the forearm locks onto the barrel, not the receiver.
steps.quote: Close the action, anchor the buttstock against your upper leg and lift outward on the forearm takedown latch.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Pivot the forearm away and off
steps.action: Keep holding the latch out. Grip the forearm and, with your left hand helping, swing its front end down and away from the barrel until it comes off. It swings off from the front. It does not slide off. If it feels stuck, check that the latch is fully out rather than pulling harder.
steps.quote: At the same time, grasp the forearm and with the help of the left hand pivot the forearm away from the barrel, removing the forearm.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Open the action, lift the barrel off the hinge pin
steps.action: Open the action again with the top lever. Now the barrel is held only by its lug sitting on the hinge pin. Carefully unhook the lug from the pin and lift the barrel up and out of the action. Go gently. The lug and the hinge pin are hand-fitted surfaces, and knocking them together is what marks them.
steps.quote: Carefully disengage the barrel lug from the hinge pin and lift the barrel upward and out of the action.
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have two pieces: the barrel, and the receiver with the buttstock. The forearm is the third. Browning says a thorough cleaning needs exactly this, and everyday care can be done with the barrel left on. Everything else in the cleaning section works from here. That means the bore and chamber from the breech, the breech face, the hinge pin, the barrel lugs and the forearm bracket.
steps.quote: More thorough cleaning requires removal of the barrel and forearm from the receiver (cleaning the barrel).
steps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions > CLEANING PROCEDURES
steps.warn: NOTICE: THE BROAD, POLISHED, FINELY FITTED SURFACES OF THE RECEIVER AND FOREARM MECHANISMS (BARREL LUGS, HINGE PIN AND FOREARM BRACKET) MUST ALWAYS BE COATED WITH A FILM OF HIGH QUALITY GREASE.

deepSteps.title: Choke tube out with the wrench
deepSteps.action: Before you touch the choke, make sure the action is open and the gun is empty. Fit the choke tube wrench and turn the tube counterclockwise to break it loose. Then unscrew the rest of the way by hand. Take the tube out at every thorough cleaning, not only when you change chokes. A tube left in too long is the one that seizes.
deepSteps.quote: Use the choke tube wrench to loosen the tube, turning it counterclockwise.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Interchangeable Choke Tube System > CHOKE TUBE REMOVAL, step 2

deepSteps.title: Clean and oil both sets of threads
deepSteps.action: Look at the threads inside the muzzle and on the tube. If they are dirty, scrub the tube with a nylon brush and gun solvent. Then give the tube and the threads a light coat of good lightweight gun oil. Browning's warning here is about seizing. Threads left dirty or dry are how a tube gets stuck in the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly oil the choke tube and threads with a high-quality, lightweight gun oil.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Interchangeable Choke Tube System > CHOKE TUBE INSTALLATION, step 2
deepSteps.warn: FAILURE TO CLEAN AND OIL THE THREADS ON THE CHOKE TUBE COULD RESULT IN THE CHOKE TUBE SEIZING IN THE BARREL.

deepSteps.title: Tube back in: fingers first, then the wrench
deepSteps.action: Screw the tube in by hand, threaded end in and notched end out, until it is finger-tight. Then use the wrench to seat it firmly. Always start by hand. A tube started with the wrench can cross-thread. Never fire without a choke tube fitted, because Browning says the barrel threads can be damaged.
deepSteps.quote: When it becomes finger-tight, use the choke tube wrench to firmly seat the tube.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Interchangeable Choke Tube System > CHOKE TUBE INSTALLATION, step 3

deepSteps.title: Ported barrels: the ports themselves
deepSteps.action: Some BT-99 barrels are ported near the muzzle, and carbon builds up in the ports. If yours is ported, scrub each port with good powder solvent on a pipe cleaner until it comes out clean. The bore patch does not reach into the ports. They need their own pass. If your barrel is not ported, skip this step.
deepSteps.quote: To clean them use a good quality powder solvent and pipe cleaners to scrub away debris.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Barrel Porting

deepSteps.title: No further — Browning stops here
deepSteps.action: Browning's own disassembly ends at the barrel and forearm. The book warns that the inner mechanism is finely fitted and can be permanently damaged by taking it apart. For anything deeper, it sends you to a qualified gunsmith or Browning's service facility in Arnold, Missouri. Adjusting the comb, buttplate and GraCoil unit is covered in the manual as fitting, not cleaning, and it is not part of this guide.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: Browning BT-99 Shotgun Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel off the receiver, and the rod always goes in from the breech end
A lightly oiled patch big enough to fit snugly, run back and forth several times
Look through the bore from both ends for lead and plastic streaks, usually near the muzzle and just ahead of the chamber
If the streaks are heavy, brass brush with powder solvent. Push the brush all the way through before you pull it back
Clean dry patch, then a final lightly oiled patch
Check that no patch is left in the barrel or chamber
Clean the chamber promptly after plastic shells. Never leave a fired hull in the chamber

cleaning.name: HINGE & LOCKUP SURFACES
tasks: Wipe the receiver, forearm and barrel metal clean with a rag
Grease film on the hinge pin, the barrel lugs and the forearm bracket. These are hand-fitted surfaces and should never run dry
A drop of oil on the forearm bracket tab
Breech faces kept clean and lightly oiled. Grit here can stop the action from closing

cleaning.name: CHOKE & PORTS
tasks: Choke tube out, then the tube and the muzzle threads cleaned with a nylon brush and solvent
Light oil on the tube and threads before it goes back in
Ported barrels: powder solvent and pipe cleaners through each port
Check now and then that the tube is still tight

cleaning.name: STOCK & FINISH
tasks: Do not flood the action with oil. It runs back into the stock wood and loosens it
Wipe the wood with a light gun oil or polish it with furniture wax, but not both
GraCoil models: now and then, clean and lightly oil the buttplate guide pins
Keep solvents, insect repellent and sunscreen off the finish

reassembly: Make sure the chamber is empty, and grease the hinge pin, barrel lugs and forearm bracket. Put a drop of oil on the tab.
Hold the grip in your right hand with the buttstock anchored between your right forearm and your side. Push the top lever fully right with your thumb and hold it there.
With your left hand, set the barrel lug's round hinge-pin recess onto the action's hinge pin.
Keep pressure on the barrel so the pin stays in its recess, then swing the barrel up to close the action. Let go of the top lever and it should snap back.
Slide the steel tab at the back of the forearm bracket into the recess in the bottom of the receiver.
Swing the forearm up tight against the barrel until you hear it click into place.
Never force the action closed. If something catches, go back to seating the hinge pin rather than pushing harder.
fncheck: First make sure the chamber is empty and point the muzzle somewhere safe. Open and close the action a few times. It should close without force, and the top lever should snap back on its own. Do not hold it with your thumb. With the action closed, push the top lever lightly to the left to feel that the breech is fully shut. Try to wiggle the forearm. It should be tight on the barrel with no play. Open the action fully and watch the extractor lift. If your gun is ported, look through the ports for any leftover pipe cleaner. Then leave the action open, the way Browning says a BT-99 should sit when you are not on the line.
